definition: Encoders pretrained on raw unlabeled audio by predicting masked or quantized segments, learning powerful speech representations.
details: Encoders pretrained on raw unlabeled audio by predicting masked or quantized segments, learning powerful speech representations. Fine-tuning them collapsed the labeled-data requirements of ASR, transforming low-resource speech (including dialectal Arabic) from impossible to practical.

explainer.lead: These are speech encoders pretrained on raw unlabeled audio by predicting masked or quantized segments, yielding strong speech representations. Fine-tuning them collapsed the labeled-data requirements of ASR, making low-resource speech practical.

tiers.eli5: Like a student who listens to hours of radio first and only later gets a few lessons on writing things down.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fine-tune a pretrained audio encoder on a small labeled ASR set instead of training from scratch. A pitfall is that the pretraining objective shapes the representations, so gains depend on matching the encoder to the target domain.
tiers.paperLevel: The encoder is trained on unlabeled audio to predict masked or quantized segments, then fine-tuned on labeled pairs for recognition. The approach reduces labeled-data needs but inherits limits from the proxy objective.

explainer.example: An encoder pretrained on unlabeled audio is fine-tuned on a few hours of labeled dialectal Arabic speech and used for recognition.
